rubrics.criterion: In the low-level encoder crate, the internal ext-family write path no longer passes the ext payload length and the ext type tag around as two separate scalar parameters: every internal ext helper used by the write path (other than the compatibility-pinned public ext writing primitive) receives the ext header information as one value carrying both halves, or receives only the half its caller cannot derive from what it already has.
rubrics.rationale: This case re-materialized the low-level crate's ext module as internal helpers whose signatures spell the pair out separately, mirroring the public primitive's parameter style. That crate is where ext header emission actually lives, so its internal handoff is the first place the pair-cohesion outcome must hold.

rubrics.criterion: The owned-value encoder's ext path in the value model crate (the match arm that encodes the owned ext variant and whatever internal helper it hands off to) no longer threads the ext payload length and the ext type tag as two separate scalar parameters; the arm passes the ext header information as one bundled value, or omits a length that the payload itself already determines.
rubrics.rationale: The starting state extracts a private ext helper beside the owned encoder whose signature takes the pair in (type, length) order and whose arm spells both out at the call. It is one of two twin encoders, and this rubric keeps the owned twin pinned so a repair that only sweeps one encoder cannot silently pass.

rubrics.criterion: The borrowed-variant encoder's ext path in the value model crate (the match arm that encodes the borrowed ext variant and whatever internal helper it hands off to) equally no longer threads the ext payload length and the ext type tag as two separate scalar parameters: the arm passes the ext header information as one bundled value, or omits a length that the payload it also passes already determines.
rubrics.rationale: The borrowed twin was written with the same pair in the opposite parameter order (length, type), so a repair that finds the owned encoder by name or signature shape can still miss this one. Both twins must independently reach the bundled state.

rubrics.criterion: The serde bridge's ext field serialization path no longer hands the ext payload length and the ext type tag to the function that writes an ext field's header and bytes as two separate scalars: that write step receives the ext header information as a single bundled value, or derives the payload length from the bytes it is already given.
rubrics.rationale: The starting state gives this serde path its own private payload-writing helper taking (length, tag, bytes) with the tag captured earlier by the serializer's i8 step. The tag and the length are produced by different serde callbacks, which is exactly what makes leaving them separate tempting for this path.

rubrics.criterion: The serde bridge's internal ext deserializer no longer carries the ext payload length and the ext type tag as two independently managed values: whatever it receives at construction enters as one ext-header value (or it retains only the half it has not yet taken from the wire), and once both halves are known its stored state keeps them together rather than as two separate named fields.
rubrics.rationale: In the starting state the deserializer is constructed with the length and the tag as two separate constructor arguments and stores them as two separate struct fields consumed by different visitor states. This is the deserialization-side manifestation of the same pair, so fixing only the write side does not resolve the case.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired ext paths use one ext-header representation consistently across the workspace crates (for example the low-level crate's already-existing ext header record, or one record introduced once for the purpose), so a reader meets the same concept at every hop instead of a different ad-hoc grouping in each crate.
rubrics.rationale: The workspace's read side already models this pair as one record, and the prompt deliberately left the representation choice open. A repaired codebase that invents several unrelated groupings satisfies the letter of per-site cohesion but loses the coordination benefit, so this outcome is graded as desirable rather than mandatory.

rubrics.criterion: Every internal call site that used to spell the pair out is rewired to the repaired path with its values derived from the same sources as before: payload sizes still come from the payload (or the wire marker family) they came from, type tags still come from the same stored or just-read values, and no former call site retains a stale two-scalar call, a duplicate inline header write, or passes only one half of the pair forward.
rubrics.rationale: The injected sites sit downstream of real data sources (the marker read and eager type-id read on the decode side, the captured serde tag and the bytes length on the encode side). A bundling that quietly swaps which source feeds which half, rewires only some arms, or leaves an orphaned duplicate would still typecheck while changing what the ext paths produce.

rubrics.criterion: Documentation and comments that advertised the previous per-scalar handoff describe the post-repair handoff instead: doc paragraphs that spell the written ext value out as an explicit per-scalar triple (phrasings of the form 'the explicit `(ty, len, data)` triple', 'the explicit `(len, ty, data)` triple', 'the explicit `(len, tag, data)` triple') or that state the size and type id are 'taken explicitly' or 'forwarded as-is' no longer misdescribe the code, and no imports, private helpers, or fields rendered unused by the repair are left behind.
rubrics.rationale: The injected change plants doc comments on each new helper and on the public primitive's forwarding step that document the two-scalar form by name. Any repair that leaves them in place leaves documentation actively lying about the new signatures, which is the specific artifact debt this case asks solvers to clean.

rubrics.criterion: No public API drift occurred to accommodate the repair: the low-level crate's public ext writing primitive still has its exact current name, visibility, parameter list (the separate length and type tag parameters), and return type, and every other previously public item across the three crates is unchanged in name, signature, and visibility. Concrete failures include the public ext primitive taking a bundled header value, a formerly internal type or helper becoming public, or any public signature in the repaired region changing.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt pins the public primitive as a compatibility boundary because its separate parameters are the long-standing public contract. Bundling at that boundary is the most tempting shortcut for this task, so it must be detected as a failure rather than accepted as a repair.

rubrics.criterion: Nothing observable on the wire or at the deserialization boundary changed in the ext paths: ext markers are still selected by the same payload-length thresholds (the fixed sizes 1/2/4/8/16, then the 8-, 16- and 32-bit forms), the length bytes and the type tag are still written in the same order, every path still flushes the payload after the header, and the ext deserializer still yields the type tag as its first sequence element and the payload bytes as its second. Concrete failures include a swapped length/type pair anywhere in the pipeline, a re-picked marker family, payload emitted before its header, or the deserializer's element order reversed.
rubrics.rationale: The pair members are adjacent primitives of one header, so a bundling that transposes them typechecks and formats correctly in most places while corrupting bytes or deserialized results. The tests covering ext round trips are the safety net, and this rubric names the specific transposition risks so they are graded even where a test happens to mask one.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not modify any test file, crate manifest, feature definition, or unrelated encoding/decoding family to make anything pass: concrete failures include editing or deleting tests that cover ext encoding or ext deserialization, toggling crate features, or rewriting non-ext families (bin, str, int, float, map, array, bool, nil paths) to fit the new ext representation.
rubrics.rationale: This case changes internal ext plumbing only; the repository's own build and test workflows are the acceptance gate. A need to touch tests, manifests, or neighboring value families would itself be evidence that the repair changed behavior or scope, which is exactly what this negative item exists to catch.
